samples.summary: No test asserts `WorkspaceScopeGuard` is actually mounted on every v1 controller, even though this delta makes it the single revocation point for keys minted by removed members
samples.evidence: This delta moves the API-key revocation guarantee into `WorkspaceScopeGuard.canActivate` (workspace-scope.guard.ts:34-38) and the guard's own spec covers the two new branches. But the guarantee only holds for controllers that carry the guard. The sibling guard has exactly this protection: `api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts:64-78` enumerates all v1 controllers and asserts `Reflect.getMetadata('__guards__', controller)` contains `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard`, with a comment explaining why. There is no equivalent test for `WorkspaceScopeGuard`, so a new (or edited) v1 controller that omits it would silently restore the pre-delta behaviour — a key minted by a removed/demoted user keeps working — with a green suite.
searchedFor: grep 'WorkspaceScopeGuard' across packages/backend (only @UseGuards decorators, api-v1.module provider, and its own spec)

samples.summary: The API-key bypass this delta removes elsewhere still exists on the image-read surface, and its test asserts the bypass rather than the new minter-membership rule
samples.evidence: `image-read.controller.ts:96-99` still returns early for `user?.isApiKey` on a workspace-id match with no `assertMember` call, and `image-read.controller.spec.ts:180` (`{ user: { isApiKey: true, workspaceId: 'w1' } }`, no `id`) encodes that as expected behaviour. Nothing in the suite covers 'API key whose minter left the workspace' for image reads, so the invariant the rest of this delta establishes (a key resolves against its minter's membership *now*) is untested and unenforced on that path. Whether that surface *should* change is the correctness lens's call; the test-side fact is that no test would notice the divergence.

samples.summary: No test covers an API key minted by a plain member acting on the minter's *own* document/folder — the allow-by-authorship half of the new rule
samples.evidence: The new API-key tests only cover two points: minter is `owner` → allowed (documents.controller.spec.ts:64-70, 226-233; folders.controller.spec.ts:167-172, 200-206) and minter is a non-author `member` → forbidden (documents.controller.spec.ts:75-81, 238-243; folders.controller.spec.ts:177-182, 208-213). Nothing exercises `req(AUTHOR, true)` with `role: 'member'`, i.e. a key whose minter is a plain member who authored the document. If the handler had been written as `member.role === 'owner'` for keys instead of `isDocumentManager(role, authorID, userId)`, every one of these tests would still pass while a legitimate CLI caller lost access to their own documents.
searchedFor: grep 'isApiKey' in packages/backend/src for every req(...) helper usage

samples.summary: Documents spec omits the 'minter left the workspace' (assertMember rejects) case that the folders spec added
samples.evidence: `folders.controller.spec.ts:215-223` adds 'refuses an API key whose minter left the workspace' by making `assertMember` reject; documents.controller.spec has no counterpart for either `remove` or `update`, only the demoted-role case. Low impact — the guard-level test (workspace-scope.guard.spec.ts:46-58) covers removal globally and the rejection would propagate loudly — but the two sibling specs are now asymmetric.

samples.summary: `req.user.id` for API keys becomes load-bearing for authorization in this delta, but `ApiKeyStrategy.validate` has no unit test; every new test fabricates the request shape
samples.evidence: All the new authorization tests build `req` by hand (`documents.controller.spec.ts:39-40`, `folders.controller.spec.ts:44-45`, `workspace-scope.guard.spec.ts:32-35`), assuming `user.id` is the minter's numeric user id. That assumption is only produced by `api-key.strategy.ts:23` (`id: apiKey.createdBy`), for which no spec file exists (no `api-key.strategy.spec.ts` under packages/backend/src/api-key). Before this delta the field was unused for keys; now `Number(req.user.id)` decides every key's authority, so a change to that mapping would leave the whole new rule silently wrong while these mocked specs stay green. `api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts` exercises the real strategy only for an owner-minted key on the happy path.
searchedFor: grep 'createdBy' across packages/backend (schema non-null, service, no strategy test)
